BiblicalUsage: The scall is a scaly sore of the head or beard, and Leviticus gives the priest a week-by-week procedure for it: look, shut up seven days, look again, shave all but the scall, shut up seven more days. The law is patient with it — the priest watches before he pronounces.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the priest's waiting is the mercy in the law: judgment is not rushed, and seven days of watching come before any word of unclean. The priest looks, waits, and looks again, because a word of unclean cannot be taken back.
